newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares up 1.32 pct despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares up 1.32 pct despite profit-taking.

text.p: Continued selective buying on the Istanbul stock market carried the index above the 1,600 resistance on Tuesday despite afternoon profit-taking which wiped out part of the earlier gains, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,607, up 21 points, or 1.32 percent higher from Monday when it soared 5.8 percent on top of last week's 3.88 percent gain caused by fading political tension. It brushed a high of 1,627 during the day.
Trade volume firmed to 44.69 trillion lira ($356.5 million) from Monday's 43.9 trillion ($350.4 million).

"The profit-taking wave in the afternoon was a normal development after the recent gains. The market may now target the index's 1,750 level after piercing the 1,600 barrier," said Tuncay Kuzu from Sahin securities.
Brokers said renewed privatisation hopes ahead of a scheduled meeting of the Higher Board of Privatisation on Thursday had fuelled buying in state firms in the morning.
